title: Smart staged-traffic calibrator and eval holdback orchestrator
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build an orchestrator that automatically calibrates staged traffic allocations for canaries/A-B experiments while preserving a statistically meaningful holdback of requests for golden evals. The goal is to reduce noisy rollouts and avoid false-positive regressions by ensuring per-cohort sample sizes meet power thresholds before advancing traffic or completing canary flips. This ticket covers the controller, the power-check heuristics, integration with existing golden prompt scorecards, and an opt-in UI flag in Console for experimental traffic calibration.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can create a staged rollout plan that adjusts traffic proportions automatically based on real-time sample variance and target statistical power
Holdback pool maintained and sampled into the eval pipeline; golden scorecards receive at least the configured min effective sample size per cohort
Automatic pause/quarantine if the eval delta on any key scorecard metric exceeds configured thresholds with p < 0.05 and minimum effect size
Ability to rollforward (increase traffic) or roll back automatically according to calibrated confidence; manual override from Console must be supported
Integration tests covering simulated traffic arrivals and evaluation scoring with deterministic seeds
Telemetry emitted: sample counts per cohort, power-estimates, pause-reasons, and time-to-decision metrics
design_notes: We will prioritize lightweight online power estimation over full Bayesian inference to keep latency and compute small inside the orchestration loop.
Use stratified sampling keyed by customer_id and route to avoid cohort bias; maintain per-cohort golden-set coverage counters
Fallback policy: if golden coverage is insufficient after N minutes, automatically route new requests to baseline model variant and flag engineering on-call
Configurable knobs: min_effect_size, min_sample_size, alpha (false positive rate), max_holdback_percent
We prefer a non-blocking holdback implementation that mirrors live traffic using async forked probes into the eval pipeline to reduce end-user latency impact
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): implement controller and unit tests; mock golden service and scoring SDK
Phase 2 (internal): deploy to dedicated staging environment; run synthetic traffic generator to validate power heuristics
Phase 3 (canary): enable on <internal-team> canary with 1% traffic and observe for 72 hours; enable auto-pause but disable auto-rollback
Phase 4 (gradual opt-in): expose feature flag in Console for customers to enable auto-calibration with conservative defaults
Phase 5 (general availability): enable default for runtime-1.22 canaries with telemetry dashboards and runbook
